title: finding(core/contract): `aspect-ratio` is the one declared layout container the curated vocabulary has never ruled on, either way
body:
Ruled: 5810240972 · letter ratified 5634038424 (aspect-ratio stays uncurated, reason recorded) · 2026-09-24T08:03Z

Filed out-of-scope by the objectui#6879 execution seat (session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`). ⛔ Recording only — no `domain:*`, no grading, no type; that is triage's to produce. ⛔ Not fixed in objectui#6879's PR: that card moves the curated roster for `box`, and curating (or refusing) a second type is a separate decision.

## The fact, measured

objectui#6879 needed a DERIVED population for its pin — "the declared container types of the JSON layout vocabulary" — instead of a hand-carried roster. The population it built is

```
LayoutSchema.options            (the runtime-enumerable zod authoring union,
                                 packages/types/src/zod/layout.zod.ts)
  ∩ ComponentRegistry meta isContainer === true
```

Measured on `origin/main` at `86ef0c764`, that population has **7 members**:

| type | in `PUBLIC_BLOCKS`? |
|---|---|
| `card` | yes |
| `container` | yes |
| `flex` | yes |
| `grid` | yes |
| `stack` | yes |
| `box` | no — objectui#6879 adds it |
| `aspect-ratio` | **no, and no card has ever said why** |

After objectui#6879 lands, `aspect-ratio` is the **only** member of that derived population outside the curated vocabulary.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a shrug

`box`'s five siblings are curated because ADR-0080's Tier B is "a thin layout/content layer". `aspect-ratio` sits in the same declared population and is simply absent — not excluded on stated merits. The distinction matters because the two states read identically from outside:

- **excluded on merits** (like `element:image`, `record:chatter`, `action:bar` — each carries its reason in `apps/console`'s `DELIBERATELY_UNCURATED`), or
- **forgotten** (like `record:line_items` in objectui#3006 and `box` in objectui#6879).

The tree does record the absence as an observable fact — `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/aspect-ratio.tsx` says, at its registration, "Not in `PUBLIC_BLOCKS`, so the react-page scope builder never saw this tag". That is a note about a consequence, not a ruling about the vocabulary.

## What the decision looks like

Two coherent answers, and the card only needs one of them chosen:

1. **Curate it** — add `aspect-ratio` to `PUBLIC_BLOCKS` Tier B. It declares four real inputs (`ratio`, `image`, `alt`, `className`) and a container slot, so it is authorable today; the catalog teaches it.
2. **Refuse it on stated merits** — e.g. "a ratio box is `box` plus a Tailwind aspect utility, and the vocabulary carries one spelling per concept" (the reasoning `element:image` already carries). Then the reason moves into the ledger entry and stops being a placeholder.

## Where it is parked meanwhile

objectui#6879's PR adds the derived pin with a **one-entry ledger**, and that entry is this issue. It is a forcing function, not a licence: the pin goes red the moment a new declared layout container is neither curated nor ledgered, and this entry is required to name a tracking issue.

## Dedupe

REST is 403 for this seat (`GitHub access is not enabled for this session`), so the sweep ran through one targeted MCP `search_issues` — declared as a channel switch. Zero hits for an `aspect-ratio` + curated-vocabulary pairing; the same call returned objectui#6879 itself, so the zero is a measurement rather than a broken query. Local `git grep` over `*.md` / `*.ts` / `*.tsx` for `aspect-ratio` intersected with `public|curat|vocabul|tier`: zero hits.

Refs: objectui#6879 (the card that measured this population) · objectui#6764 (declared the containment) · ADR-0080 (the curated contract)
